Subject: Session ops: aligning prompt specs, fallback routing & load-test window

Hi Devin / Sara —

Thanks again for confirming the POC scope. Before we lock calendar slots I want to align on three operational items so the hands-on prompt lab delivers useful signal:

1) Prompt inventory: can you confirm the two canonical flows you want covered (customer support triage + upsell classification)? If there are priority prompt sets, can you flag which ones must be in the first run vs. optional?

2) Structured-output & guardrails: we’ll propose a structured-output schema (JSON with status, category, score) plus model-level guardrails for hallucination thresholds. Laura will share a short template — please confirm any required fields.

3) Fallback routing & load-test window: we want to exercise model fallbacks under burst load. Proposed window: Tue April 20 10:00–12:00 PT for a 2-hour staged load test (can tighten). Do you need a different time or another region?

Attached: prompt_inventory_v2.xlsx (draft), routing_fallback_matrix.csv (sample), session_agenda.docx

Proposed next steps:
- Devin: confirm priority prompt sets and any blackout times by EOD Thu
- Sara: confirm whether Netzo needs additional network prep or proxy IPs
- Laura/Jonas (cc): we’ll pull a staging config and can toggle quantization profiles during the test

If that matches your expectations I’ll send calendar invites and a short runbook.

—Ben
Ben Carter

This looks good. Quick answers:
- Priority prompt sets: 1) triage (highest), 2) NPS/feedback classification (secondary), 3) upsell (optional). I flagged the rows in the attached prompt_inventory_v2.xlsx with an "X" in the first_run column.
- Structured output: please include a transaction_id and source_channel in the schema — we need to join outputs back to our event logs.
- Load window: Apr 20 10–12 PT works, but Devin (we) are on call for coverage 11–13 PT. Could we shift to 11–13 PT to overlap?

Two small asks:
1) Can Redwood supply a short runbook with failure-mode checks (timeouts, fallback counts) so our infra can monitor?
2) If possible, run a quick baseline of latency at small batch sizes before the big window.

I attached the annotated prompt inventory.

Thanks —
Devin

Ben / team —

Attached is the structured-output template (pasted below) and a short guardrail checklist. I also uploaded a smoke-test script to the shared Drive link Ben added.

Structured-output (example fields):
- transaction_id (string) — required
- source_channel (string) — required
- status (enum: ok, needs_review, failed)
- category (string) — taxonomy (triage/nps/upsell)
- score (float 0-1)
- model_version (string)
- fallback_reason (optional string)

Guardrail checklist:
- Max tokens per response: 512
- Hallucination threshold: prompt-specific; flag if >0.15 adverse content score
- Confidence score below 0.3 -> route to fallback model
- Limit single-session request rate to 10 rps per user during test

Jonas — for the runbook: please include the exact monitoring queries we’ll use (p99 latency, fallback count, error rate by model) and attach the smoke-test.sh. If you want I can take the first pass at the monitoring dashboards.

Devin / Sara — once you confirm the shifted baseline time (10:45 vs 10:30) we’ll post the final invite.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: structured_output_template.json (schema text, 2KB); guardrail_checklist.txt (text, 1KB); smoke-test.sh (bash script, 3KB)
